theorem.name: Capacity Monotonicity Theorem
assumptions: capacity vectors are ordered componentwise C <= C_prime
every capacity-constrained resource coordinate is included as a minimized Pareto objective
all other objective coordinates are capacity-independent for the compared plans
theorem.statement: Pareto(C) is a subset of Pareto(C_prime)
proof_sketch: let p be Pareto-optimal under C
assume a newly considered q under C_prime dominates p
dominance implies every resource requirement of q is <= the corresponding requirement of p
p is feasible under C, so r(p) <= C
therefore r(q) <= r(p) <= C, so q was already feasible under C
q would already have dominated p under C, contradiction

monotonicity_can_fail_when: latency/traffic/error values change as a function of capacity or runtime pressure
resource peak coordinates are omitted from the Pareto objective
the candidate plan semantics themselves change with capacity
important_caveat.research_consequence: static activation topology and runtime-pressure behavior must remain separate evidence planes
